formulas.name: Single-source distances
formulas.where: The Bellman optimality conditions that every algorithm solves; the shortest-path predecessors of \(v\) are the nodes \(u\) attaining the minimum (Bellman 1958).

formulas.name: Dijkstra relaxation (Dijkstra 1959)
formulas.where: Correct for non-negative lengths; bidirectional Dijkstra runs it from both ends. Breadth-first search (Moore 1959) is the unit-length case; Delta-stepping (Meyer and Sanders 2003) is a parallel bucketed variant.

formulas.name: Bellman-Ford with negative lengths
formulas.where: Converges within \(n-1\) rounds when no negative cycle is reachable from the source; a change in round \(n\) signals a negative cycle (Goldberg and Radzik 1993 is a heuristic improvement). Potentials \(p\) with \(\ell+p(u)-p(v)\ge0\) reweight lengths.

formulas.name: A* (Hart, Nilsson and Raphael 1968)
formulas.where: Expands nodes by \(f\); returns a shortest path when \(h\) is admissible (and, for closed-set variants, consistent). The distance is the same as Dijkstra's; only the nodes expanded differ.

variants.paths_sssp: Shortest-path lengths from one source by Delta-stepping; infinity for unreached nodes (an optional cutoff turns longer distances into unreachable).
variants.paths_multi_source: The smaller of the distances from several sources: \(\min_{s\in S}d(s,v)\).
variants.paths_predecessors: For each node the set of predecessors on shortest paths from the source: \(u\) with \(d(s,u)+\ell(u,v)=d(s,v)\).
variants.paths_negative: Distances under possibly negative lengths (Bellman-Ford, Goldberg-Radzik, shifted or reweighted lengths), or a negative-cycle signal.
variants.paths_astar: The shortest path found by A* with an admissible heuristic; the distance equals that of Dijkstra.
variants.paths_bidirectional: The shortest path by searching from both ends; the distance is the same, only the work differs.
variants.ord_astar: A* shortest path between two nodes.
variants.ord_bellman_ford: Bellman-Ford distances or path from a source, tolerating negative lengths without negative cycles.
variants.ord_bidir_bfs: Bidirectional breadth-first search: the shortest unweighted path between two nodes.
variants.ord_bidir_dijkstra: Bidirectional Dijkstra: the shortest weighted path between two nodes.
variants.ord_dijkstra: Dijkstra's single-source distances or path for non-negative lengths.
variants.cat_path_retrieve_shortest: Documented for BCT as retrieving a shortest path; not recorded in detail.
